title: Float-mount a print on a hidden riser, centred on the backing board
instruction: Float-mount the print on the white backing board. First lay the black riser flat on the board, then lay the print face up on top of the riser, centred on the board with its long side along the board's long side. The riser must end at least 1 cm in from every edge of the print, so that it cannot be seen. Then let go and move both grippers away.
context: What is measured is a set-back: with the print laid on, a 10 mm card strip must slide its full width under every edge of the print without meeting the riser, and the print must sit centred and square on the backing. Lying as it comes, this riser runs across the print and is exactly as long as the print is wide, so it passes only if it is turned a quarter turn and laid lengthwise. Framers float-mount prints with deckled or signed edges on a hidden riser (a stack of mat board) so all four edges show and cast a shadow; the riser is set back from every edge by at least its own height (here 10 mm), so the print's edge hides it from any view steeper than 45 degrees. Done in frame shops, galleries and museum mount rooms; a riser that shows and a print off centre are the commonest float-mount faults. The order is not scored as a rule: the end state forces it (a print on the bare board cannot float).
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Three objects; nothing else is on the table. (1) Backing board: white acid-free foam board on a rigid base (sRGB 0.95, 0.95, 0.93), a plain box 180 mm along x, 130 mm along y and 5 mm thick, fixed to the table (tape it down for real trials), centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0, so it spans x 21.0 to 39.0 cm and y -6.5 to +6.5 cm; its top is 5 mm above the table. It has no marks. (2) Riser: a black (sRGB 0.05, 0.05, 0.05) stack of mat board glued into one rigid block, 70 x 30 x 10 mm, 15 g, loose, lying flat on the table centred at x 24.0 cm, y -36.0 cm, with its 70 mm length along y and its 30 mm width along x (it spans x 22.5 to 25.5 cm, y -39.5 to -32.5 cm). (3) Print: a print dry-mounted on 10 mm rigid foam-centred board (gatorboard), so it stays flat; cream face (sRGB 0.93, 0.89, 0.78); 110 x 70 x 10 mm, 22 g, loose, lying face up on the table centred at x 24.0 cm, y +36.0 cm, its 110 mm sides along x and its sides square (it spans x 18.5 to 29.5 cm, y +32.5 to +39.5 cm). The print has no top or bottom edge. Nominal end state: the riser centred on the board with its 70 mm length along x (top 15 mm above the table), the print centred on it, long side along x (underside 15 mm, face 25 mm above the table): the riser is then 20 mm in from every edge of the print, and the margins are 35 mm along x and 30 mm along y. With a straight-down grip only the right arm reaches the riser and only the left arm reaches the print: each arm's straight-down reach near the table ends about 15 cm past the midline at x 24 cm, and each part's nearer edge is 32.5 cm past it. Both arms reach the board.
scoring: Read every control step (20 Hz). 'At rest': over the last 0.5 s (10 control steps) the part's centre moved along a path shorter than 5 mm and it turned less than 3 degrees. 'Riser set': the riser lies flat (its 10 mm axis within 10 degrees of vertical, either broad face down), its lowest point is 3 to 7 mm above the table (on the board's top, 5 mm up), its whole outline seen from above is on the board, and it is at rest. 'Print floating': the print is face up (its face normal within 3 degrees of straight up), at rest, its lowest point is 13 to 17 mm above the table (on the riser's top, 15 mm up), and the riser's centre lies inside the print's outline seen from above. 'Inset': in the print's own frame, the smallest signed distance from any corner of the riser's outline seen from above to any edge of the print's outline (negative when a corner sticks out; nominal 20 mm; about 0 for the riser laid across the print, as it starts). 'Off centre': the plan distance from the print's centre to the board's centre. 'Turned': the angle between the print's 110 mm sides and the board's 180 mm sides, folded to 0 to 90 degrees (half a turn counts as square; a quarter turn is 90). 'Clear': both grippers' finger pads, however turned, are at least 30 mm from the print and the riser (tips 30 mm straight above the print are clear). 'Off the table': a loose part's lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top. Score 0 if a part is off the table or the riser is not set (nothing done; riser left on the table, on the print, on its edge or end, past the board's edge or still moving; left-arm-only demo). Otherwise 0.25 if the print is not floating (right-arm-only demo; print on the bare board, held above the riser, tipped, face down, or so far off that the riser's centre is not under it). Otherwise 1.0 if the inset is 10 mm or more, off centre 6 mm or less, turned 3 degrees or less, and clear; 0.75 if the inset is 10 mm or more, off centre 12 mm or less and turned 8 degrees or less, but 1.0 is not met (e.g. 9 mm off centre, turned 5 degrees, or a gripper holding or near a part); 0.5 in every other case (the riser laid as it lies, across the print: its ends are flush with the print's long edges, so it shows; the print turned a quarter turn to cover it; over 12 mm off centre; turned over 8 degrees; inset under 10 mm). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends with success once the 1.0 conditions have held for 1 s; otherwise the score is read from the last step at the run limit with the same rules (no hold needed). There is no whole-trial or order rule: a part pushed or dropped into place is scored as it ends. Real trial, before touching anything: slide a 10 mm wide card strip under each edge of the print along its whole length (it must go in its full width everywhere without meeting the riser: inset); read the four margins with a steel rule (off centre: half the differences of opposite margins, combined) and the turn with a square against the board's long edge; read the float height at an edge with a rule; then lift the print off and check that the riser lies flat with its whole outline on the board.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one friction for all contacts. The board is fixed; the riser and print are loose and rest by gravity only (a real float mount glues the riser to the backing and hinges or glues the print to it; not modelled). The print is mounted on 10 mm rigid board, so it stays flat; masses are those of mat board and gatorboard. Whether the riser shows is scored from geometry (the inset), not from rendered views. The scorer reads the parts' poses and the grippers' finger positions.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the riser back flat on the table centred at x 24.0 cm, y -36.0 cm with its 70 mm length along y, and the print back face up on the table centred at x 24.0 cm, y +36.0 cm with its 110 mm sides along x. The backing board stays taped in place.
